name: matches the reported Airbnb example and accepts either optimal order
input: the four tasks from the 2025-02 interview report
test:
tasks = [('a', 2, 8), ('b', 1, 3), ('c', 2, 5), ('d', 3, 3)]
snapshot = list(tasks)
order, total_reward = deadline_reward_schedule(tasks)
assert total_reward == 16
assert order in (['c', 'a', 'd'], ['a', 'c', 'd'])
assert tasks == snapshot

name: accepts either equal-reward optimum without an invented ID tie-break
input: two equal-reward tasks competing for day one plus a later task
test:
tasks = [('b', 1, 5), ('a', 1, 5), ('later', 2, 1)]
order, total_reward = deadline_reward_schedule(tasks)
assert total_reward == 6
assert order in (['a', 'later'], ['b', 'later'])

name: selects the unique optimal subset under deadline collisions
input: five tuple tasks with a collision on day one
test:
tasks = [('a', 4, 70), ('b', 1, 80), ('c', 1, 30), ('d', 2, 100), ('e', 3, 40)]
snapshot = list(tasks)
order, total_reward = deadline_reward_schedule(tasks)
assert total_reward == 290
assert set(order) == {'a', 'b', 'd', 'e'}
assert len(order) == 4
deadlines = {task_id: deadline for task_id, deadline, _ in tasks}
assert all(day <= deadlines[task_id] for day, task_id in enumerate(order, start=1))
assert tasks == snapshot
